reports.title: Novia Delima
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The Trust had adopted the Manchester triage system but due to demand on the ED the time identified through the triage system could not be met
very young babies present significant challenges in diagnosis and early clinical input by a clinician experienced in dealing with young children was important
concerns.hazard: diagnostic challenges for very young babies

concerns.quote: the ED on call consultant arrangements meant that long wait times would not in themselves trigger on call consultants being asked to attend the hospital

reports.title: Harry Richford: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: recruited as a locum registrar by the Hospital Trust without there appearing to have been any assessment of his skills and abilities or any supervision of him at the hospital
concerns.hazard: locum registrar without assessment or supervision

concerns.quote: current policy of the East Kent Trust states that it is the responsibility of the healthcare professional who will be supervising the locum to assure themselves of his/her competence
concerns.hazard: lack of competence assurance for locums

concerns.quote: had worked two night time shifts at the QEQM before the night of Harry's birth
concerns.hazard: lack of feedback on locum competence

concerns.quote: risk to the life of both mothers and babies if there is a lack of clarity as to the processes or the need to take prompt action where it is necessitated in the event of an obstetric concern or emergency developing
concerns.hazard: lack of clarity in obstetric emergency processes

concerns.quote: There appeared to be from the evidence given at the inquest substantial confusion amongst staff as to when a consultant should be called at night.
concerns.hazard: staff confusion about consultant escalation timing

concerns.quote: current contracts at the East Kent Trust permit consultants to live up to 30 minutes travel time from the hospital
concerns.hazard: delayed response to night time emergencies

reports.title: Felix Hartley: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: over the weekend and overnight Neonatology Consultants are not available immediately on site at either the Princess Royal Hospital, Haywards Heath or the Royal Sussex County Hospital in Brighton
concerns.hazard: delayed access to on-call neonatology consultants

concerns.quote: on-call Consultant cannot be more than 30 minutes from either Brighton or Haywards Heath
concerns.hazard: inadequate proximity of on-call consultant to emergency sites

concerns.quote: no national guidance as to the time that an on-call Neonatology Consultant should be expected to attend a hospital in the event of an emergency or as to whether multiple sites can be covered by one on-call Consultant

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that consultants may be located more than 30 minutes away from the hospital, which can delay emergency response. They describe the same hazard of excessive travel time affecting timely consultant attendance.
links.earlier_quote: The current contracts at the East Kent Trust permit consultants to live up to 30 minutes travel time from the hospital.
links.later_quote: the Trust practice, as opposed to Policy, is that the on-call Consultant cannot be more than 30 minutes from either Brighton or Haywards Heath.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight delays in getting an on‑call consultant to attend when needed. The earlier report focuses on wait‑time thresholds not triggering a call, while the later report notes distance and travel constraints that can cause similar delays.
links.earlier_quote: the ED on call consultant arrangements meant that long wait times would not in themselves trigger on call consultants being asked to attend the hospital.
links.later_quote: The on-call Consultant does not always have access to an emergency vehicle and if called to attend either site would use their own vehicle

links.explanation: Both reports highlight uncertainty about when to summon a consultant during out‑of‑hours periods. The earlier report notes that long ED waits do not automatically trigger consultant attendance, while the later report describes staff confusion about the criteria for calling a consultant at night.
links.earlier_quote: the ED on call consultant arrangements meant that long wait times would not in themselves trigger on call consultants being asked to attend the hospital.
links.later_quote: There appeared to be from the evidence given at the inquest substantial confusion amongst staff as to when a consultant should be called at night.
